extra_misconceptions.fact: High-frequency RF energy penetrates deeply and heats underlying tissue rapidly, often causing severe internal burns before pain registers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Radio frequency burns on the skin behave identically to standard household 60 Hz alternating current shocks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unbonded ground rods allow dangerous voltage differences through the soil during a strike, so all ground rods must be bonded together.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Driving a separate ground rod for a radio tower without connecting it to the main house ground is the safest lightning setup.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Lithium-ion thermal runaway generates its own oxygen, requiring class ABC or dry chemical extinguishers and large volumes of cooling water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pouring water on a burning lithium-ion battery immediately extinguishes the chemical reaction inside the damaged cells.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High-voltage filter capacitors retain lethal direct current charges long after power-off and must be discharged with a grounding stick.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Turning off a high-voltage linear amplifier power switch makes the internal filter capacitors immediately safe to touch.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a lightning surge when an exterior antenna ground rod is not bonded to the home electrical service ground?
Why is it dangerous to touch an ungrounded radio chassis while your other hand rests on a grounded metal water pipe?
Which physical indicator on a lithium-ion battery pack signals internal gas buildup and an immediate thermal runaway hazard?
What measurement confirms that an AC wall outlet's third-prong ground terminal actually provides a low-impedance path to earth?

extra_misconceptions.fact: All electromagnetic waves in a vacuum travel at the speed of light, approximately 300,000,000 meters per second, regardless of frequency.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Higher frequency radio waves travel through free space at a faster speed than lower frequency radio waves.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High Frequency spans 3 to 30 megahertz, whereas Very High Frequency spans 30 to 300 megahertz and hosts FM broadcast stations.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The High Frequency band extends from 30 megahertz up to 300 megahertz and includes FM commercial broadcast radio.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hertz units measure how many electromagnetic wave cycles pass a fixed point each second, while watts measure transmitter output power.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Kilohertz and megahertz measure the audio loudness or output wattage of a radio transmitter rather than its wave oscillation rate.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard AM broadcast stations in the United States transmit in the Medium Frequency band between 535 and 1,705 kilohertz.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard AM broadcast radio stations operate inside the High Frequency shortwave spectrum above 3 megahertz.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the physical wavelength of a radio wave in meters when you multiply its operating frequency in megahertz by ten?
Where should a Scout position the boundary line between High Frequency and Very High Frequency on a logarithmic spectrum chart?
Why must a half-wave dipole antenna cut for the 2-meter VHF band be much shorter than one built for the 40-meter HF band?
Which specific frequency band between 300 kHz and 3,000 kHz hosts commercial AM broadcast stations alongside maritime beacons?

extra_misconceptions.fact: VHF and UHF waves normally pass straight through the ionosphere into space, limiting direct communication to near line-of-sight distances.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: VHF and UHF handheld radio signals routinely refract off the ionosphere to provide reliable communication across oceans.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Solar ionization strengthens the F2 layer during daylight hours, supporting long-distance skywave skip on higher HF bands like 15 and 20 MHz.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Daytime solar ultraviolet radiation weakens the ionosphere and prevents all shortwave skywave propagation on 10 and 15 MHz.

extra_misconceptions.fact: WWV and WWVH transmit continuous standard time tones and geophysical solar indices on 2.5, 5, 10, 15, and 20 MHz to test band openings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stations WWV and WWVH broadcast only local weather forecasts for Colorado and Hawaii rather than global propagation data.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ground waves hug the curvature of the Earth best at lower frequencies like LF and MF, while UHF signals are rapidly absorbed by terrain.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ground wave signals travel further at UHF microwave frequencies than they do at Low Frequency or Medium Frequency wavelengths.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the ionospheric D and F layers after sunset that allows distant HF stations to be heard thousands of miles away?
Why does a strong signal on 15 MHz from WWV in Fort Collins indicate that upper HF bands are open for long-distance skip?
Under what condition does a silent skip zone form between the end of an HF station's ground wave and its first skywave hop?
Which physical barrier limits two VHF handheld transceivers to line-of-sight range when no repeater is mounted on a hilltop?

extra_misconceptions.fact: True CW transmission switches the unmodulated radio frequency carrier completely on and off to form dots and dashes within a narrow bandwidth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Continuous wave Morse code modulates an audio tone onto a steady carrier wave just like an AM broadcast transmitter.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Frequency modulation keeps the carrier amplitude constant while shifting the instantaneous carrier frequency above and below its center.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Frequency modulation varies the height and power envelope of the transmitted radio wave in step with the microphone audio.

extra_misconceptions.fact: At full modulation, a conventional AM signal wastes two-thirds of its total power in the steady carrier and splits the rest into two sidebands.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard full-carrier AM places nearly all of its transmitter wattage into the voice sidebands rather than the carrier.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth encode digital binary data onto microwave radio frequencies in the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz spectrum bands.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth signals use acoustic sound waves rather than radio frequency electromagnetic waves to send digital packets.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the carrier and opposite sideband in a Single Sideband transmitter that makes it more efficient than standard AM?
Why does an FM receiver reject static bursts from nearby lightning strikes much better than an AM receiver tuned to the same area?
Under what condition does Continuous Wave Morse code penetrate heavy atmospheric noise when voice signals become unreadable?
Which method lets Bluetooth devices in the 2.4 GHz band avoid interference by switching channels 1,600 times per second?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Block diagrams show high-level functional stages connected by signal-flow arrows, while schematic diagrams show exact electronic components.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A station block diagram displays every individual resistor, capacitor, and transistor pin connection inside the transceiver.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The outer shield of coaxial cable confines RF energy inside the feedline so power reaches the antenna without radiating inside the station.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Coaxial feedline is supposed to radiate radio energy all along its length on the way from the transceiver to the antenna.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An RF amplifier boosts radio frequency signal wattage between the transceiver and feedline, whereas an audio amplifier drives the speaker.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Connecting an external linear RF amplifier between the antenna and the speaker increases the audio volume in the room.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Resistors use a jagged zigzag line to represent ohmic resistance, while inductors use looped coils to represent magnetic energy storage.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Schematic symbols for inductors and resistors are interchangeable because both components oppose current flow in identical ways.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should a Scout position an external RF power amplifier and SWR meter along the signal path between a transceiver and antenna?
Why must a technician inspect a schematic diagram rather than a block diagram when replacing a burned resistor inside a power supply?
What happens to transmitter final transistors when a coaxial feedline is disconnected or shorted while keying at full RF power?
Which specific schematic symbol distinguishes a polarized electrolytic capacitor from a variable tuning capacitor or an inductor?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The FCC regulates non-federal radio and interstate communications inside the United States, while the ITU coordinates international treaties.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Federal Communications Commission has legal jurisdiction to issue licenses and enforce radio rules in every country worldwide.

extra_misconceptions.fact: In the United States, broadcast stations east of the Mississippi usually start with W, while western stations usually start with K.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Commercial broadcast call signs beginning with the letter K are assigned exclusively to stations east of the Mississippi River.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard ITU phonetics like Alfa, Bravo, and Charlie are chosen so each word remains distinct across accents and heavy radio interference.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Making up custom words like Apple, Boy, and Cat during an emergency net works just as well as the standard ITU phonetic alphabet.

extra_misconceptions.fact: FCC Part 97 rules require amateur stations to transmit their assigned call sign every ten minutes during a communication and at its conclusion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Amateur radio operators in the United States are only required to announce their call sign once at the start of a two-hour net.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must United States amateur radio operators identify with their FCC-assigned call sign at least every ten minutes during a contact?
What geographic detail does the single digit in a call sign like W1AW or K6BSA originally indicate in the United States?
Under what condition does spelling a call sign with the ITU phonetic alphabet prevent errors that rhyming letters cause over static?
Which international agency coordinates global frequency allocations so signals crossing borders do not jam foreign radio services?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A phone's GPS chip is a passive receiver that measures arrival time differences of atomic-clock signals broadcast from orbiting satellites.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Smartphones transmit signal bursts up to orbiting GPS satellites so the satellites can calculate where the hiker is standing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard cellular calls require a base station cell site and backhaul network to route full-duplex traffic between two mobile handsets.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Two standard smartphones out in the wilderness can talk directly to each other like walkie-talkies without any cell tower.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Airplane Mode disables the phone's radio frequency transmitters to prevent interference with aircraft navigation and save battery power.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Enabling Airplane Mode only dims the phone screen while leaving the cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth transmitters active.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cell sites often fail during disasters when commercial power and backup generators run out, fiber lines are cut, or call channels saturate.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cell towers stay operational indefinitely during major wildfires or hurricanes because they never rely on commercial grid power.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a smartphone's battery drain and transmitter output when you hike into a canyon with no cellular tower coverage?
Why must a smartphone GPS receiver lock onto at least four satellites to calculate both three-dimensional location and altitude?
Under what condition do cell networks fail during a disaster while battery-powered amateur VHF simplex radios keep working?
Which mechanism allows a cellular network to reuse the same UHF frequencies across a city without calls interfering with one another?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The FCC eliminated all Morse code testing requirements in 2007, so Technician, General, and Amateur Extra exams test written theory and rules.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Passing the FCC Technician class amateur radio exam requires sending and receiving Morse code at twenty words per minute.

extra_misconceptions.fact: FRS radios are license-by-rule up to two watts with permanently attached antennas, whereas GMRS requires an FCC license and allows repeaters.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Family Radio Service walkie-talkies require an individual FCC license test and allow high-power external roof antennas.

extra_misconceptions.fact: FCC Part 97 strictly prohibits music broadcasts and pecuniary interest on amateur bands, reserving the service for noncommercial communication.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Licensed amateur radio operators are permitted to broadcast commercial music or accept payment for delivering business messages.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mayday is reserved strictly for grave and imminent danger to life or vessel, whereas Pan-Pan indicates an urgent safety situation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Calling Mayday is used for routine radio checks on amateur repeaters, while Pan-Pan means a life-threatening emergency.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your HF operating privileges when you upgrade from an entry-level Technician license to a General class license?
Why must a Scout listen carefully and ask if a frequency is in use before calling CQ or joining a repeater QSO?
Which five details belong in a station logbook entry when logging a ten-minute QSO during a Jamboree on the Air session?
What do the three digits in an RST signal report of 599 tell the transmitting operator about readability, strength, and tone?

extra_misconceptions.fact: FCC Part 97 rules strictly prohibit pecuniary interest on amateur bands; commercial work requires a commercial license or certification.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Holding an FCC Amateur Extra license permits an operator to accept direct payment for commercial radio broadcasts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Radio frequency engineers, avionics technicians, and satellite systems specialists remain in high demand across wireless industries.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern radio careers are limited to on-air broadcast announcers because streaming services replaced terrestrial radio.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Public service communicators deploy only when officially activated by a served agency or net control to maintain site safety and order.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Volunteer amateur radio operators can self-dispatch into disaster zones as soon as they hear an emergency on a scanner.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An unmodulated carrier wave still radiates full radio frequency power and can cause severe RF burns unless the transmitter is locked out.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Commercial transmitter antennas are safe to climb whenever audio programming is silent because no RF energy is radiated.

extra_socratic_questions: What protocol must an amateur operator follow before transmitting emergency traffic on a local ARES or RACES net?
Which legal authority distinguishes a Civil Defense RACES station from a voluntary ARES emergency communications net?
What measurement confirms that a broadcast transmitter tower meets FCC radio frequency exposure limits for crew?
Why is it dangerous to service a commercial broadcast antenna without verifying transmitter lockout and RF power?
